# Exact Credit Along Strong Routes: Forward-Only Pretraining with Boost → Cut

*Draft. Numbers marked [pending] wait on runs in the queue. Tables are generated by `collect.py`, figures by
`llm-slop-review/figures.py`; PAPER.md tracks the experiment matrix.*

## Abstract

Forward-only learning rules train a network without a backward pass. They measure how the loss changes when the
network is perturbed. On the Noise benchmark, the leading rule is Dust. It estimates every layer's credit from noisy
end-to-end perturbations over large populations. We show that the credit of a well-chosen counterfactual network
can be **measured exactly**, up to the finite-difference step, at a cost far below Dust's. The measurement has to
follow structure that trained networks already have. Two observations drive the method:
1. A loss that depends on one token's stream can be probed along a full orthogonal cycle of directions without
   interference from other tokens.
2. A trained network's function rides on each input's strongly active units, so a perturbation only needs to travel
   through those units.

**Boost → Cut** has two phases:
- **Boost** is stagewise: every sub-block learns against the shared head reading the stream right after it.
- **Cut** is end-to-end. It measures exact *attention-cut* credit, carried only through each token's top 6% of MLP
  units. Its keys come from single-key experiments evaluated in closed form.

On the benchmark's 38M-parameter GPT, trained on 10M tokens for one epoch, Boost → Cut reaches held-out test loss
**3.935 ± 0.012** (3 seeds) in 7.3 minutes on 8×H100. The Dust record reaches 3.999 ± 0.025 in 72 minutes on the same hardware, and Boost → Cut uses 24× fewer matrix FLOPs. From 7.3M to 243M
parameters, Boost → Cut trails backprop by a roughly constant 0.23–0.26 nats [243M final configuration pending]. The
On a plain GPT (GELU, no value embeddings or skip scalars), the route shortcut fails because GELU spreads each
token's work over most units; with all units, the gap to backprop is 0.32 nats, at 2.0× the time, and Boost → Cut
still beats Dust (4.224 against 4.367). The stagewise head start is what concentrates credit onto few routes, which is why the route
restriction is nearly free:
it costs 0.005 nats of exact-credit loss after the head start and 0.028 without it. Boost → Cut still uses about 136×
backprop's FLOPs. An oracle with exact attention-cut credit puts 0.19 of its 0.23-nat gap to backprop on the
attention cut itself.

## 1. Introduction

**Why forward-only.** A learning rule that only runs the network forward needs no reverse dataflow. That matters for
hardware that cannot run a backward pass (analog, optical or neuromorphic accelerators) and as a model of learning in
brains. It need not save memory: our method keeps the clean pass's activations and evaluates large batches of probes
(Section 6). The Noise benchmark (Gülbahar et al. 2026) makes the question concrete. It fixes the model,
the data, the epoch and the score, and asks for the best learning rule that never runs a backward pass. Its records
use Dust (qlabs.sh/research/dust), which jitters every layer of a large virtual population and correlates the
resulting losses with the jitter.

**The cost of exact credit is the width of the measurement, not the depth of the network.** For a site of W
dimensions, W orthogonal perturbations of one token's stream measure that token's credit there exactly, up to the
finite-difference step. Population methods pay for interference: every token's loss responds to every other token's
perturbation through attention, and that cross-talk is what forces large populations and noisy estimates. Remove the
interference and a full cycle of W probes per token per site suffices.

**Contributions.**
1. **Per-token, interference-free measurement.**
   - In Boost, each readout loss is a function of one token's stream.
   - In Cut, every attention output is held at its clean value, so each token is its own experiment.
   - Keys are measured by single-key experiments, evaluated in closed form.
2. **Strong routes.** Each perturbation travels only through the token's strongly active MLP units, 128 of 2,048
   per block. Restricting the routes costs 0.006 nats of measured test loss and saves 2.4× the time.
3. **A head start that concentrates credit.** The stagewise phase leaves the network with fewer, stronger routes. At
   matched loss, the route-restricted credit agrees with the full credit at cosine ≥ 0.98 with the head start, against
   0.92–0.95 without (Section 5).
4. **A careful comparison.**
   - 3 seeds for the main cells, and a held-out test split.
   - Every measured credit checked against autograd of its estimand.
   - Counted FLOPs.
   - Ablations of every design choice, and two standard forward-only baselines.
   - Scaling from 7.3M to 243M parameters, a second dataset, and a plain GPT.

**Results in brief.** On the benchmark (Figure 1, Table 1):
- Boost → Cut beats the Dust record by 0.063 nats (p = 0.032) in about a tenth of the time.
- It beats both of its own phases run alone (by 0.049 and 0.127 nats; p = 0.007 and p < 0.001 over 3 seeds), and
  both forward-only baselines by a wide margin.
- It trails backprop with the same optimizer by 0.23 nats.

## 2. Setting

**The benchmark.**
- **Model.** The Noise GPT: 8 pre-norm blocks of width 512 and 37.7M parameters, with:
  - relu² MLPs of width 2,048;
  - value embeddings on alternate blocks;
  - QK-norm and rotary positions;
  - learned residual and embedding-skip scalars;
  - a logit soft cap at 15;
  - half-sequence attention windows in three of every four blocks (full windows in the fourth and the last).
- **Data.** 4,880 FineWeb sequences of 2,048 tokens (10M predictions), one epoch.
- **Score.** Mean next-token cross-entropy on the 544-sequence validation set.
- **Rule.** No autograd (reverse or forward mode) and no hand-written backward pass; learning signal comes from
  evaluating the model forward.

**Our line, stricter than the benchmark's letter.**
- Every learning signal is a change of a loss caused by a perturbation, measured by running the network forward.
  The measurement is either at the site it trains or one local step from such a measurement (for example, from a
  measured credit at a block's output to the weights that write it).
- Credit is never carried through weights, attention or skip connections by formula or by finite differences beyond
  that one step.
- Noise reduction is allowed: orthogonal draws, masks, kernels, regression and pooling.
- Appendix A lists every component, how it meets the line, and every judgment call.

**Protocol.**
- **Held-out test split.** It continues the benchmark's FineWeb stream one pool further, exactly as the Dust
  repository defines its `test.pt` (544 sequences; sha256 `cb7a29f0…`).
- **Selection.** Every design choice was made on validation. Headline numbers are test loss of the final weights, and
  validation is reported alongside.
- **Seeds.** Each seed changes the initialization and every estimator's random stream; the data order is the
  benchmark's. Main cells have 3 seeds; we report mean ± standard deviation.
- **Compute.** Wall-clock is measured on Modal 8×H100 nodes. It varies between runs of identical code and settings:
  seed 0 of the final configuration took 394 s once and 456 s another time, on different nodes. We therefore also
  count matrix FLOPs per training token.

## 3. Method

The model, initialization, optimizer and schedule are the Noise record's: ANVIL II on the block matrices, Adam
elsewhere, linear warmdown over the last 30% of the epoch. Only the credit changes.

### 3.1 Boost: stagewise credit, measured exactly

**Objective.** Each attention and each MLP is a stage of gradient boosting. It is trained only to lower the loss of
the shared head reading the residual stream right after it: the logit lens as a training objective.

**Measurement.** A readout loss ℓ_t(x_t) is a function of token t's stream alone, so its gradient is measured by
forward differences along a full sign-flipped Hadamard cycle {h_j}, j = 1…W:

  g_t = Σ_j [ℓ_t(x_t + s h_j) − ℓ_t(x_t)] / s · h_j / W,  with step s = 0.005 · RMS(x_t).

Every probe is the actual soft-capped cross-entropy of the actual head, with the moved stream's RMS norm evaluated
exactly. The head is linear before its norm, so all W probes of all tokens are one broadcast over cached logits.

**What learns from the measured credit.**
- **Writers** (the output projections) get credit ⊗ input.
- **MLP hidden units** take one local step from the measured credit through relu², along a full cycle over each
  token's top H/8 units.
- **Queries** use the record's local search against the attention output's measured credit, a full cycle per head.
  **Keys** use single-key experiments (Section 3.3).
- **Values, gates and value embeddings** use the record's sampled local search with a matched filter.
- **The embedding** is measured at the first attention stage, along each token's own path: the other positions' keys
  and values are held at their clean values.
- **Mixing scalars** use central differences of their stage's loss.
- **The head** uses the record's coordinate differences at every readout.

### 3.2 Cut: attention-cut credit along strong routes

Phase 2 measures end-to-end credit. A move of token t's stream at site d runs forward through every later block to
t's own loss, with two things held at their clean values:
1. **Every attention output.** The move then reaches only t's loss, so tokens are independent experiments.
2. **Every MLP unit outside t's top k by output contribution** (|relu²(h_i)| · ‖W_out[:, i]‖). The move then travels
   only along t's strong routes.

**Sites and moves.**
- A full cycle per token at the raw embedding and at every block's mid stream measures the attention-cut credit there.
- Block outputs reuse the same moves: a move of block d's output is a move of block d+1's mid stream times its
  residual scalar.
- The top stream is probed through the head alone.
- The mixing scalars are measured by ±h moves through the same chain (central differences).

**Exact differences, not linearization.** Each move is carried as an exact difference from the clean forward:
- rms-norm differences in closed form;
- relu² differences as (a − b)(a + b);
- logit changes through the head's linearity.

Nothing is linearized: the chain computes f(x + δ) − f(x) of the counterfactual network, restricted to k units per
block. Its agreement with autograd (cosine 0.9996–0.9999) shows that the step is small enough for the differences to
match the directional derivatives.

**What learns from the measured credit.** Writers, MLP hidden units and the attention internals take one local step,
as in Boost. The internals are scored against c_proj's view of the mid-stream credit.

### 3.3 Keys by single-key experiments

Moving one key k_t changes every query's attention in exactly one logit, so the new output is evaluated from the
clean probabilities in closed form:

  o′_s − o_s = (a′ − a)(v_t − o_s) / (1 − a + a′),  with a′ = a·exp(Δl_st).

This is the construction the Noise record already uses for its head (coordinate differences, one logit at a time).
All T × d_head experiments per head are evaluated in bulk, and each query's change is scored against its target.

One numerical detail matters. The processed key's change has to be formed exactly before the logit product.
Otherwise TF32 rounding (~1e−3 relative) is as large as the move's whole effect. Computed this way, the keys match
autograd of their local step at cosine 1.000.

### 3.4 The handoff

- **Boost** runs for the first 30% of the epoch at 4 sequences per update, two GPUs per sequence.
- **Cut** runs for the rest at 8 sequences per update, one per GPU.
- **Carried over:** the weights, ANVIL's rails and Adam's moments.
- **Schedules:** each phase follows the schedule of a one-phase run at the same fraction of the epoch.

### 3.5 Cost

Per token, compared with backprop's 0.264 GFLOP:

| phase | matrix FLOPs per token | × backprop | where the cost goes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boost | 29.0 G | 110× | W·(2L + L) readout probes, each a soft-capped cross-entropy over the 4,096-word vocabulary (50M vocabulary entries per token) |
| Cut | 38.8 G | 147× | (L + 1)·W chain moves through k units per block, plus one head evaluation each (21M vocabulary entries per token) |

**How the cost scales.** Per token, backprop costs about 6 × 12·L·W² FLOPs. Cut makes (L + 1)·W moves, and each
travels through up to L blocks of k ∝ W units, plus one head evaluation of W·V. Its cost relative to backprop
therefore grows like L·W/4 + V. The vocabulary term V dominates at 38M (L·W/4 = 1,024 against V = 4,096). At 243M
the two terms are equal (4,096 each), and Cut costs 227× backprop (371 against 1.64 GFLOP per token). Boost's cost
is dominated by its vocabulary probes, so its ratio falls with size instead (54× at 243M). Boost → Cut is 136× at 38M
and 175× at 243M.

## 4. Experiments

### 4.1 Main result

**Table 1.** 38M, held-out test loss, mean ± sd over 3 seeds (wall-clock is the seeds' mean on 8×H100).

| method | test | val | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Boost → Cut** | **3.935 ± 0.012** | 3.946 ± 0.013 | 438 s |
| Cut alone (no head start) | 3.984 ± 0.010 | 3.995 ± 0.009 | 503 s |
| Boost alone | 4.062 ± 0.007 | 4.072 ± 0.006 | 342 s |
| Dust record (16k population) | 3.999 ± 0.025 | 4.009 ± 0.026 | 4,312 s |
| local losses + forward gradient (128 directions) | 4.292 | 4.305 | 474 s |
| direct feedback alignment (best of four learning rates) | 5.253 | 5.265 | 139 s |
| backprop, same model, init and optimizer | 3.706 ± 0.009 | 3.712 ± 0.009 | 31 s |

The benchmark's own backprop baseline (Adam with a learning-rate cooldown) reaches 3.769 validation loss. Our
backprop row uses the record's optimizer and is stronger.

**Learning rates** (seed 0). Every method uses the record's rates, scaled together:
- **Backprop** is best at the record's rates: test 3.764, 3.701, 3.725 and 3.860 at ×0.5, ×1, ×2 and ×4.
- **Boost → Cut** is best there too: 4.064, 3.937 and 3.967 at ×0.5, ×1 and ×2.
- **The baselines** get their best rate of the sweep: forward gradient ×1 (×0.5: 4.355), and DFA ×0.1 (×1: 5.439,
  ×0.3: 5.264, ×0.03: 6.262).

**Significance** (Welch's t-test on test loss over 3 seeds each):
- **the head start:** Boost → Cut beats Cut alone by 0.049 (95% CI 0.023–0.074, p = 0.007);
- **the end-to-end phase:** Boost → Cut beats Boost alone by 0.127 (95% CI 0.101–0.152, p < 0.001);
- **against Dust:** Boost → Cut beats the Dust record by 0.063 (95% CI 0.011–0.116, p = 0.032). The record's own
  log (val 3.991 in 4,303 s) matches our seed 0 (val 3.992 in 4,292 s).

**Figure 1** (`fig_curves.png`): validation loss along the epoch for Boost → Cut, its two phases alone, the Dust
record and backprop.

**Official log.** Seed 0 with the benchmark's script interface has validation 3.9448, re-scored by `utils/eval.py` as
3.94481, in 456 s (`submission/boostcut_track1_log/`). The current Track 1 record is 3.991.

### 4.2 Ablations

**Table 2.** 38M, seed 0 unless noted. All rows keep Boost's keys sampled, against their own 3-seed base. The oracle
column trains with exact autograd credit of the same estimand (validation loss).

| variant | test | val | time | oracle (val) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **base: 30% switch, top-128 routes, exact Cut keys** (3 seeds) | **3.945 ± 0.003** | 3.956 ± 0.003 | 434 s | 3.910 |
| switch 0% (Cut alone) | 3.979 | 3.992 | 503 s | 3.955 |
| switch 50% | 3.980 | 3.989 | 422 s | 3.938 (all units) |
| switch 100% (Boost alone) | 4.113 | 4.122 | 338 s | 4.060 |
| routes: top 64 (3% of units) | 3.967 | 3.976 | 434 s | 3.928 |
| routes: top 256 (12.5%) | 3.935 | 3.945 | 489 s | |
| routes: all 2,048 units | 3.939 | 3.948 | 1,021 s | 3.905 |
| Cut's keys sampled (the record's search) | 3.969 | 3.980 | 464 s | |
| Boost's keys exact too (the final configuration; 3 seeds) | 3.935 ± 0.012 | 3.946 ± 0.013 | 438 s | |

**Findings.**
- **Routes are the speed lever.** Top-256 matches the unrestricted credit at half the time. Top-128 costs about
  0.006 for a 2.35× speedup.
- **The 30% head start beats both no head start and a 50% switch,** measured and at the oracle.
- **Exact keys matter in Cut** (0.025). In Boost alone they matter as much (4.062 ± 0.007 against 4.113 with
  sampled keys), but after the handoff the difference is within seed noise (3.935 ± 0.012 against 3.945 ± 0.003).

**Figure 2** (`fig_time.png`): test loss against wall-clock for every method (left), and Boost → Cut's design space
(right).

### 4.3 Baselines

- **Local losses with forward gradients** (Ren et al. 2023). This is Boost's stagewise objective with random
  directions instead of full cycles: 128 orthogonal directions per token per readout, a quarter of the cycle. It
  reaches 4.292 against 4.113 for Boost alone with full cycles. The comparison isolates exact measurement from
  sampling at the same objective.
- **Direct feedback alignment** (Nøkland 2016; Launay et al. 2020 for transformers). This is Cut with every site's
  credit replaced by a fixed random projection of the exact output error, e·B_site with B_site ~ N(0, 1/V). Everything
  one local step from those credits is Cut's.
  - At the record's learning rates it is unstable: the loss spikes to 12–14 twice and settles at test 5.439.
  - Its best rate (×0.1) is stable but reaches only 5.253: random feedback does not train this transformer.

### 4.4 Where the remaining gap is

Oracles train with exact autograd credit of each estimand, under the same schedule (validation loss, seed 0):

| credit | val | step |
|---|---|---|
| backprop (true gradient) | 3.708 | |
| … with Boost's 30% head start | 3.711 | the head start costs backprop nothing |
| exact attention-cut credit after the head start, all units | 3.905 | +0.195: the attention cut |
| … top-128 routes | 3.910 | +0.005: the routes |
| measured: Boost → Cut (3 seeds) | 3.946 ± 0.013 | +0.036: measurement (sampled values and gates, one-sided steps) |

The attention cut is the main cost: credit that reaches a site only through later attention is dropped. The routes
are nearly free after the head start, and the measurement costs about 0.04.

### 4.6 Beyond the benchmark: another dataset and a plain GPT

**TinyStories** uses the same tokenizer. Training takes the first 10M tokens of its train split; validation and test
are the first and second 544 sequences of its validation split. Model 38M, seed 0:

| | test | val |
|---|---|---|
| Boost → Cut | 1.633 | 1.685 |
| backprop | 1.508 | 1.558 |
| Dust record | [pending] | |

The gap to backprop is about half of FineWeb's.

**A plain GPT** (`analysis/plain_gpt.py`).
- **Removed:** relu² (now GELU), the value embeddings, the embedding skips and residual scalars, the soft cap, and
  the short windows (now full causal attention everywhere).
- **Kept:** pre-norm, the parameter-free RMS norm, rotary positions, QK-norm and the untied head. The model has 29M
  parameters.
- **Method changes:** only the architecture-specific pieces. The routes rank units by |GELU(h)|·‖W_out[:, i]‖.
- **Dust, adapted the same way:** GELU blocks and an uncapped head. Every hidden unit is jittered, because GELU has no
  dead units.

| plain GPT, seed 0 | test | val | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boost → Cut, top-128 routes | 4.560 | 4.573 | 475 s |
| Boost → Cut, all 2,048 units | 4.224 | 4.240 | 938 s |
| Dust record recipe | 4.367 | 4.383 | 3,633 s |
| backprop, same optimizer | 3.909 | 3.916 | 23 s |

**With the route shortcut, the method does not transfer.**
- The gap to backprop grows from 0.23 to 0.65.
- Cut's phase stalls: validation goes 4.73, 4.68, 4.72, 4.79, 4.72 and 4.63 over its six evaluations, where the
  benchmark model falls steadily from 4.45 to 3.99.

**Why: GELU spreads the work, and the routes lose the credit.** `analysis/route_fidelity.py` applies one measure to
both models: the minimum over sites of the per-token cosine between the route-restricted and the full attention-cut
credit.
- **Benchmark model:** the top 128 units carry the credit at cosine 0.98–0.99 at every checkpoint from the switch
  on, and at most 202 of 2,048 units carry 90% of a token's MLP output.
- **Plain GPT:** the top 128 units carry it at 0.90 at the switch, falling to 0.61 by the end; even the top 512
  reach only 0.68. The units carrying 90% of the output grow from 697–840 at the switch to as many as 1,523.
- **A feedback loop:** training on the restricted credit makes the plain GPT denser, and that makes the restriction
  worse.

**Without the shortcut, most of the loss comes back.** With all 2,048 units, Boost → Cut reaches test 4.224, and Cut
improves at every evaluation. The gap to backprop is 0.32, against 0.23 on the benchmark model, at 2.0× the time of
the routed run. The strong-route shortcut needs sparse activations; the rest of the method carries over.

**Dust loses ground too.** The Dust record's recipe reaches 4.367 on the plain GPT, with a gap to backprop of 0.46
against 0.29 on the benchmark model. Boost → Cut with all units beats it by 0.144 in about a quarter of its time.

## 5. Why strong routes, and why a head start

Cammarata (2026) argues that a trained network's function rides on each input's strongly active units, and that
early structure ("head starts") decides how a network organizes. We measure both on our runs with
`analysis/clean_probe.py`. Each checkpoint of Boost → Cut (seed 1) and of Cut alone is compared at matched validation
loss.

**Table 4.** Minimum over sites of the per-token cosine between the attention-cut credit restricted to each token's
top-k MLP units and the full credit. Each row pairs a checkpoint of Boost → Cut with the checkpoint of Cut alone
nearest to it in validation loss (checkpoints every 488 sequences, so the losses differ by up to 0.05); Figure 4 shows
every checkpoint.

| val loss (with / without) | with head start, k = 64 / 128 / 256 | without | units carrying 90% of a token's MLP output, blocks 1–7 (with / without) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.750 / 4.798 | 0.968 / 0.989 / 0.999 | 0.867 / 0.930 / 0.975 | 99–162 / 145–256 |
| 4.368 / 4.343 | 0.954 / 0.985 / 0.998 | 0.858 / 0.934 / 0.980 | 82–191 / 82–209 |
| 4.273 / 4.253 | 0.954 / 0.986 / 0.998 | 0.863 / 0.941 / 0.985 | 70–193 / 71–195 |
| 4.002 / 4.044 | 0.939 / 0.980 / 0.997 | 0.868 / 0.946 / 0.987 | 71–203 / 68–182 |

**Figure 4** (`fig_routes.png`).

**Findings.**
- With the head start, the top 128 of 2,048 units carry the credit at cosine ≥ 0.98 throughout Cut's phase.
  Without it, the same units carry it at 0.93–0.95. This is why the route restriction costs 0.005 at the oracle after
  the head start and 0.028 without.
- Boost leaves block 0's MLP nearly silent: 7–22 units carry 90% of its output, against 91–274 without the head
  start. It also inflates the saliency coordinate that Cammarata describes (peak 1.8k–3.1k against 0.8k–1.7k).
- The head start does not help backprop (oracle 3.711 against 3.708). Its value is specific to measurement along
  routes: it makes the network easier to measure.

## 6. Compute

- **Per token** (Section 3.5): Boost → Cut ≈ 35.8 GFLOP, 136× backprop. The Dust record uses 876 GFLOP (3,316×), so
  Boost → Cut needs 24× fewer matrix FLOPs.
- **Wall-clock gap to Dust:** about 10×. The forward-only probes are dominated by elementwise soft-capped
  cross-entropies over the vocabulary, which FLOP counts miss.
- **Memory**, peak on one GPU for one sequence (`analysis/memory.py`, weights included, optimizer state excluded):
  - backprop: 0.80 GiB;
  - Boost: 3.49 GiB;
  - Cut: 3.57 GiB.

  The forward-only phases use about 4.4× backprop's memory. The probe batches set it: their chunk size
  (2²⁷ elements) trades memory for speed.
- **The whole study**, including development, used about [pending] H100-hours on Modal, of which [pending] were for
  this paper's runs.

## 7. Related work

- **Perturbative learning:**
  - node and weight perturbation;
  - Dust; evolution strategies and EGGROLL;
  - SPSA; MeZO (zeroth-order fine-tuning).
- **Forward gradients:** Baydin et al. 2022; Ren et al. 2023 (local losses with forward gradients, our closest
  baseline); Fournier et al. 2023.
- **Local losses and greedy layer-wise training:**
  - Hinton 2006 and Bengio 2007: greedy layer-wise pretraining, then fine-tuning. Boost → Cut is this recipe with
    forward-only measurement in both phases.
  - Belilovsky et al. 2019; Nøkland & Eidnes 2019; Löwe et al. 2019.
  - Deep supervision (Lee et al. 2015); the logit lens (nostalgebraist 2020) and tuned lens (Belrose et al. 2023).
- **Feedback alignment and synthetic credit:**
  - Lillicrap et al. 2016; DFA (Nøkland 2016); DFA for transformers (Launay et al. 2020);
  - synthetic gradients (Jaderberg et al. 2017); target propagation; Forward-Forward (Hinton 2022).
- **Interpretability and learning dynamics:**
  - Cammarata 2026, *Neural Networks Are Already Clean*;
  - gradient starvation (Pezeshki et al. 2021); coherent gradients (Chatterjee 2020);
  - massive activations (Sun et al. 2024).

## 8. Limitations

- **Attention credit.** The attention cut drops credit that reaches a site only through later attention. That costs
  0.19 nats at the oracle and is the main remaining gap to backprop.
- **Sampled internals.** Values, gates and value embeddings are still sampled. Measuring them exactly in our line
  reduces to the transposed-attention product, which the line excludes.
- **Compute.** About 136× backprop's FLOPs and about 14× its wall-clock on the same hardware. Forward-only here means
  no backward pass, not cheaper training.
- **Architecture.** The route shortcut needs sparse activations. On a plain GPT with GELU it fails (gap 0.65), and
  without it the gap is 0.32 at 2.0× the time (Section 4.6). The method as tuned
  depends on the benchmark model's features.
- **Breadth.** Two datasets, up to 243M parameters, and 10M tokens. Longer training and larger models are untested.
- **Seeds.** 3 seeds for the main cells; the ablations and the scale and generality cells have one.
- **Wall-clock** varies by up to 16% between runs of identical code. FLOP counts are the stable comparison.
- **Memory.** About 4.4× backprop's peak per sequence at 38M; forward-only does not mean less memory here.

## 9. Conclusion

Measured exactly, credit is affordable along the routes a trained network already uses. A stagewise head start makes
those routes few. The remaining gap to backprop is mostly credit through attention.

---

## Appendix A: the rules, component by component

**The line.** No autograd and no hand-written backward pass. Every learning signal is a change of a loss caused by a
perturbation, measured by running the network forward, either at the site it trains or one local step from such a
measurement. Noise reduction (orthogonal draws, masks, kernels, regression, pooling) is allowed. Credit is never
carried through weights, attention or skip connections by formula or by finite differences beyond that one local
step. This is the line the Noise records follow: the record's attention internals are one local step from a measured
attention-output target.

| component | signal | how it meets the line |
|---|---|---|
| Boost readouts | forward differences of each token's actual soft-capped head loss along a full Hadamard cycle of the stream | measured at the site; the head's linearity only reuses W·x |
| Boost writers, MLP hidden, embedding stage | credit ⊗ input; one local step through relu²; own-path first-stage rerun | one local step; the frozen context is disclosed |
| Boost mixing scalars | central differences of their stage's loss | measured |
| Cut chain (embedding, mid streams) | forward differences of each token's own loss, with moves run through later blocks | measured end to end in a counterfactual network: attention outputs held, and each token's weak MLP units held |
| Cut block outputs | the same moves, relabeled | no new computation |
| Cut mixing scalars | ±h moves of each scalar, through the same chain | measured |
| queries | full cycle per head through the attention rerun, scored against the target | one local step |
| keys | single-key experiments in closed form, scored against the target | one local step; the record's coordinate-head construction |
| values, gates, value embeddings | the record's sampled local search with a matched filter | one local step |
| head | the record's coordinate differences | the record's |

**Judgment calls, disclosed.**
1. Holding attention outputs (Cut), and the other positions' keys and values (Boost's embedding stage), at their clean
   values during a move.
2. Holding each token's weak MLP units at their clean outputs (Cut's routes).
3. Scoring the attention internals against c_proj's view of the mid-stream credit. This equals scoring their moves
   through c_proj.
4. Using the clean attention pattern for the values' matched filter, like the record's decay kernel.
5. The intermediate readouts are a training objective (the logit lens), not a change to the model.

## Appendix B: every measurement against autograd

`analysis/test_boostcut.py`. Cosine between the measured credit and autograd of the same estimand: the
route-restricted attention-cut loss for the chain, and for keys their local step against the same targets. The chain
sites are the raw embedding and every mid stream. The production route budget is k = H/16; "all units" lifts the
restriction. The 38M check uses the final weights of a trained Boost → Cut run (`hybrid_cutk_f0.3`). The others use
initial weights.

| model | k | chain sites at k | chain sites, all units | top stream | mixing scalars | exact keys (Cut and Boost) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38M (trained: `hybrid_cutk_f0.3`'s final weights) | 128 | 0.9996–0.9999 | 0.9999 | 1.000 | 1.000 (ratio 1.004) | 1.000 |
| 7.3M (init) | 64 | 0.9964–0.9994 | 0.9999–1.0000 | 1.000 | 1.000 (ratio 0.993) | 1.000 |
| 243M (init) | 256 | 0.9922–0.9997 | – | 1.000 | 1.000 (ratio 0.980) | 1.000 |
| plain GPT, 29M (init) | 128 | 0.9985–0.9999 | 0.9999–1.0000 | 1.000 | – | 1.000 |

## Appendix C: settings

All presets share these settings. Width-dependent values are fractions of the MLP width H.

| | value |
|---|---|
| optimizer | the Noise record's: ANVIL II on block matrices (lr 0.023, wd 2.25), Adam elsewhere (lr 0.003; embeddings ×300, mixing scalars ×30), betas (0.7, 0.95), linear warmdown over the last 30%; polar margin 1.1 |
| data order | the benchmark's (permutation seed 1); one epoch of 4,880 sequences of 2,048 tokens |
| Boost | 4 sequences per update, two GPUs per sequence; readout step 0.005·RMS (one-sided, full cycle); MLP hidden: top H/8 units, step 0.05·RMS; queries 64 draws per head (a full cycle); keys exact (step 0.003·RMS); values 512 draws, gates 64 (sampled, matched filter); value embeddings from value draws; embedding at the first attention stage along its own path; mixing scalars by central differences (step 0.01); head by coordinate differences at every readout |
| Cut | 8 sequences per update, one per GPU; chain step 0.01·RMS (one-sided, full cycle) at the raw embedding and every mid stream; routes: top H/16 units by output contribution; mixing scalars by ±0.01 moves through the chain; internals as in Boost, against c_proj's view of the mid-stream credit; head by coordinate differences at the final readout |
| switch | after 30% of the epoch (366 Boost updates, then 427 Cut updates) |

## Appendix E: verification

The ledgers in `ledger/` tie every number in this paper to the runs that produced it:
- Each run is tied to its exact command, data, checkpoint hash and billed cost, and, for later runs, to a snapshot of
  the code that ran.
- `ledger/verify.py` recomputes every printed number from the run records and fails on any mismatch, rounding
  included (`ledger/verification.md`).
- Every finished checkpoint is re-scored from its weights alone by `analysis/ledger_rescore.py`. The benchmark model
  is also scored by the official `utils/eval.py`. All re-scores agree with the logged losses to within 1e-7.
- Compute is summed from Modal's billing export, app by app (`ledger/compute.md`).

`ledger/README.md` explains each check and what the ledgers cannot show.

torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 train/boostcut/run.py --preset 38m --seed 0 --test-file test.pt

torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 analysis/dust_preset.py --preset 38m --seed 0 --test-file test.pt
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 analysis/plain_gpt.py --preset 38m --seed 0 --test-file test.pt
python analysis/test_boostcut.py --preset 38m [--arch plain]
python analysis/flops.py --preset 38m --methods backprop,boost,cut,dust
